brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Built a compact cluster: full bases piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0 and piece:1,-1,0, plus a north half base piece:0,1,0 (half-n). check_build reports ok with meshClash clear. Two joint bolts were added to lock the bases. No desk props or cover details were added, so 'desk unit' is only the structure.
drawer:0#0,1#cut sits on the cut face of the half base piece:0,1,0 (added via the drawer socket, default classic style).

requirements.requirement: A spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 at the junction of cells (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0), the three bases that meet there. Its type is mount, because a solid spike refused a platform.

requirements.requirement: The spike holds a small platform
requirements.evidence: setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on that mount spike (accepted, no warnings).

finish.summary: Built a compact cluster of four bases with a drawer on the half base's cut face and a mount spike at the three-base corner carrying a small platform. check_build is ok with meshClash clear; the only remaining notice is an info-level OPEN_CAP_FACE, which I left unaddressed. The desk-unit requirement is partial because I did not add any desk-specific dressing or covers.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
